stemOverrides.81: The area of the region bounded by the curve \(y=\big||x-1|-2\big|\) and the line \(y=2\) is ____.

authoredSolutions.72: The line \(x-y=0\) has slope \(1\); \(x+2y=3\) has slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\); \(2x+y=6\) has slope \(-2\). The acute angle between the first and second satisfies \(\tan\theta=\left|\frac{1-(-1/2)}{1+1\cdot(-1/2)}\right|=3\), and between the first and third \(\tan\theta=\left|\frac{1-(-2)}{1+1\cdot(-2)}\right|=3\). Two equal angles make the triangle isosceles. Hence (C).
authoredSolutions.81:
Substitute \(u=x-1\), so the curve becomes \(y=\big||u|-2\big|\); the answer is the same because a horizontal shift does not change area.

Find where the curve meets \(y=2\): \(\big||u|-2\big|=2\Rightarrow |u|-2=\pm 2\Rightarrow |u|=4\) or \(|u|=0\). So the line touches the curve at \(u=-4,\ 0,\ 4\).

On \([0,4]\): for \(0\le u\le 2\), \(y=2-u\); for \(2\le u\le 4\), \(y=u-2\). The curve dips to \(y=0\) at \(u=2\) and rises back to \(y=2\) at \(u=4\). By symmetry the shape on \([-4,0]\) is the mirror image, so the required area is
\[\text{Area}=2\int_{0}^{4}\big(2-y\big)\,du.\]

Compute the two pieces:
\[\int_{0}^{2}\big(2-(2-u)\big)\,du=\int_{0}^{2}u\,du=2,\qquad \int_{2}^{4}\big(2-(u-2)\big)\,du=\int_{2}^{4}(4-u)\,du=\Big[4u-\tfrac{u^{2}}{2}\Big]_{2}^{4}=8-6=2.\]

Thus \(\int_{0}^{4}(2-y)\,du=2+2=4\), and the total area \(=2\times 4=8.\)
